headline: Pellridge Foods misses interest payment on term loan
body: Pellridge Foods Ltd missed a scheduled interest payment on its term loan at the end of October, according to a notice sent to its lenders. The chilled-meals maker said it was in talks with its banks about a standstill. Finance director Owen Harrowby said trading had been hit by higher energy costs at its two kitchens.

headline: Sallowmere opens distribution warehouse
body: Sallowmere Building Supplies Ltd has opened a 12,000 square metre distribution warehouse to serve builders' merchants in the north of the region. The company said the site would add 40 jobs by the spring. Managing director Clara Wexcombe said orders from housebuilders had held up through the summer.

headline: Supermarket group sues Halden over spoiled stock
body: A regional supermarket group has filed a lawsuit against Halden, claiming that a refrigeration failure at one of its depots spoiled frozen stock worth 2.4 million. The claim, lodged in the commercial court last week, also says Halden waited three days before telling customers about the fault. Halden said it would defend the claim.

headline: Northwind loses its largest customer
body: Northwind has lost its largest customer, a national parcel carrier that accounted for about a third of its revenue, people familiar with the matter said. The carrier will move the work to another provider from January. Northwind declined to comment.

headline: Agency cuts Northwind rating on refinancing risk
body: A credit rating agency cut Northwind (NYSE: NWEG) by one notch to BB+ on Tuesday, citing the cost of refinancing bonds due in 2028. The agency said cash flow from the gas storage business had weakened. Northwind said the downgrade did not affect its bank facilities.

headline: Quillfield Engineering to buy Fenmoor Analytics
body: Quillfield Engineering Ltd agreed to buy Fenmoor Analytics, a privately held maker of vibration-monitoring software, for 18 million. Quillfield said it would pay from cash and an existing bank facility. Fenmoor's 30 staff will join Quillfield's controls division.

headline: Tolland Packaging wins supermarket tray contract
body: Tolland Packaging (NYSE: NWEG) won a three-year contract to supply recycled food trays to a national supermarket chain, the company said on Monday. The contract is worth about 9 million a year.

headline: Central bank holds rates
body: The central bank of the Republic of Valdora kept its policy rate at 4.25 percent on Thursday. Governor Ilse Tormund said inflation was easing but that wage growth was still too high. The bank will publish the minutes in two weeks.

headline: Elmstead Creameries enters administration
body: Elmstead Creameries, a cheese and butter maker, entered administration on Wednesday after failing to refinance its debts, with 120 jobs at risk. Administrators said they would look for a buyer for its two creameries. Ferncastle Dairy Ltd, which competes with Elmstead in the regional cheese market, said its own supply contracts and finances were unaffected. Ferncastle expects to take on some of Elmstead's supermarket orders.

headline: Flood warning lifted for Halden
body: The river authority lifted its flood warning for Halden on Sunday after water levels fell overnight. Roads into the town centre reopened in the afternoon, and the council said no homes had been flooded.
